archetypes.name: stale-token-sweep
archetypes.rationale: The plan promises a completeness grep gate but lists only 13 specific files; other skill docs, agent definitions, TSV projections, and CHANGELOG may silently retain the retired token.
archetypes.prompt_body: Hunt exhaustively for the exact retired `--simple` argv token and the `cancelled-tier-gate` outcome string across every file type the plan's completeness gate targets (`*.md`, `*.sh`, `*.json`, `*.txt`, `*.tsv`, `*.toml`) — especially in files outside the 13-file plan list, such as other skill SKILL.md files, `.claude/skills/`, `skills/shared/`, agent definitions, `larch-logs/`-adjacent tooling, and any CHANGELOG or topology projection. Cross-check whether any file embeds the retired token as a test fixture needle, help-text literal, or cross-skill example that would survive the completeness grep because it is excluded by the exclusion list. If a file outside the plan's file list contains either string on a live surface, that is a plan defect—the file list is incomplete and the completeness gate will not catch it. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: test-contract-verifier
archetypes.rationale: The plan removes several test assertions but adds no new assertion that `--simple` now triggers the generic hard-error-before-Step-0 path, leaving the retired flag silently swallowed if the generic rejection is not actually wired.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that the three updated test harnesses (`test-design-structure.sh`, `test-design-driver.sh`, `test-render-final-summary.sh`) together contain at least one needle that pins the generic disallowed-flag rejection behavior the plan relies on to stop the retired `--simple` token from being treated as positional text. Check whether any of the removed assertions (duplicate-tier mutual-exclusion, `simple_row` table-row grep, `cancelled-tier-gate` outcome) were the only tests guarding a behavior that still needs coverage under the new model, such as default-SIMPLE resolution when no tier flag appears. Also confirm that the replacement default-SIMPLE tier-resolution assertion added to `test-design-structure.sh` is specific enough that a regression reintroducing the interactive tier gate would cause the test to fail rather than pass vacuously. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: outcome-consumer-audit
archetypes.rationale: The plan traces `cancelled-tier-gate` removal through only five files but does not audit run-log parsers, the audit-runs skill, or any reporting harness that reads SUMMARY_OUTCOME values from committed larch-logs.
archetypes.prompt_body: Search for `cancelled-tier-gate` as a string consumer — not just a producer — across run-log parsing scripts, the `audit-runs` skill, `scripts/render-run-summary.md`, any `.awk`/`.py`/`.sh` that reads SUMMARY_OUTCOME from larch-log files, and any CI or harness that validates the outcome enum. A stale consumer expecting this outcome will silently misparse historical run logs or produce a runtime error on the next design run that reaches what used to be the gate. Confirm the plan's claim that the interactive tier gate is the sole producer by grepping the skill scripts and Step 0b code path for any emit, echo, or printf that outputs the `cancelled-tier-gate` string outside the five listed files. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
